breed.name: German Shepherd
breed.metabolic_type: Large breed, high energy, predisposed to sensitive digestion, exocrine pancreatic insufficiency (EPI), gastric dilatation-volvulus (GDV / bloat), and hip/joint dysplasia.

protein.description: High-quality, highly digestible animal proteins (chicken, lamb, turkey, beef, fish) are essential for maintaining lean muscle mass and supporting high activity levels.

fat.description: Essential fatty acids (Omega-3 and Omega-6, EPA, DHA) for cognitive development, skin health, double coat maintenance, and joint inflammation reduction.

carbohydrates.recommended_source: Easily digestible complex carbs such as sweet potato, brown rice, oats, and quinoa.
carbohydrates.avoid: Excessive corn, wheat, or soy fillers which can trigger sensitivities or gas.

fiber.description: Moderate fiber promotes optimal stool consistency, vital for GSDs prone to sensitive digestion.

micronutrients_and_supplements.name: Glucosamine & Chondroitin
micronutrients_and_supplements.purpose: Joint support for large breeds prone to hip and elbow dysplasia.

micronutrients_and_supplements.name: Omega-3 Fatty Acids (EPA/DHA)
micronutrients_and_supplements.purpose: Anti-inflammatory support for joints, skin barrier function, and coat gloss.

micronutrients_and_supplements.name: Probiotics & Prebiotics
micronutrients_and_supplements.purpose: Gut health support, crucial for managing sensitive GSD stomachs and preventing dysbiosis.

puppy.feeding_frequency: 3 to 4 meals per day until 6 months, then 2 meals.
puppy.focus: Controlled growth rate to prevent developmental orthopedic diseases (DOD).

adult.focus: Maintenance of lean muscle, weight management to protect joints.

senior.focus: Easily digestible proteins, joint support, lower calorie density if less active, kidney support.

dietary_recommendations: Feed 2-3 smaller meals daily instead of one large meal.
Avoid vigorous exercise 1 hour before and after meals.
Use slow-feeder bowls to prevent gulping air.
Supplement with powdered pancreatic enzymes prior to every meal.
Novel protein sources (venison, duck, salmon) if chicken/beef intolerance is suspected.

items.name: Carrots
items.prep: Raw or steamed, cut into bite-sized pieces

items.name: Green Beans
items.prep: Plain, fresh or frozen (steamed or raw)

items.name: Plain White or Brown Rice
items.prep: Fully cooked, unseasoned (great for upset stomachs)

items.name: Plain Greek Yogurt
items.prep: Unsweetened, low fat, in moderation (check for lactose tolerance)

items.name: Chocolate
items.reason: Contains theobromine and caffeine, highly toxic to dogs.

items.name: Grapes and Raisins
items.reason: Can cause sudden acute kidney failure.

items.name: Xylitol (Artificial Sweetener)
items.reason: Causes rapid insulin release, leading to severe hypoglycemia and liver failure.

items.name: Onions, Garlic, Chives
items.reason: Contains thiosulfate which damages red blood cells and causes Heinz body anemia.

items.name: Macadamia Nuts
items.reason: Causes weakness, tremors, hyperthermia, and vomiting.

items.name: Alcohol & Yeast Dough
items.reason: Causes ethanol poisoning and severe gas accumulation / bloating.

items.name: Cooked Bones
items.reason: Splinter easily, causing internal punctures or gastrointestinal blockages.

items.name: Avocado
items.reason: Contains persin (especially in pit, skin, and leaves), causing vomiting and diarrhea.

items.name: Coffee, Tea, Caffeine
items.reason: Stimulants that can cause heart palpitations, tremors, and seizures.

items.name: Citrus Fruits (Lemon, Lime, Grapefruit)
items.reason: High levels of citric acid and essential oils cause digestive upset.

items.name: High-Sodium and Fatty Foods
items.reason: Can trigger acute pancreatitis, especially dangerous for GSDs.
